as_told.title: Eric Hecker's South Pole neutrino emitters claim

plain: IceCube, a large detector for tiny particles called neutrinos buried in the ice at the South Pole, is said by a man named Eric Hecker to be able not only to detect but to send out energy, and the story's title links it to earthquakes, with Christchurch in New Zealand named among the places. A guest named Jay Anderson tells Michels that Hecker has found documents that "insinuate it's a two-way device" whose energy "can be used to actually emit". Michels tells it himself, without the documents, as Hecker's claim that "there are neutrino detectors and emitters on the South Pole". If true, a science instrument would double as a weapon.
